_meta.purpose: Single source of truth for WHICH agents get spawned for a given code unit. Read by project workflows AND by Claude when triaging manually -- one table, not two drifting copies.
_meta.core_principle: Triggers are evaluated by CODE (path globs + import greps), never by an extra LLM triage call. A triage agent per unit would itself cost tokens and defeat the purpose.

(2) Same three moved C->T: not needed on ~99% of projects (only 1-4 of 8 projects even carry the required stack tag), and even on a project where relevant, must not fire per-file/per-entrypoint or ride along in a consensus roster -- spawn only when the task genuinely IS ML-pipeline / DB-schema / SEO work. architect/code-architect moved C->B (now per-unit-triggered, bundled with group A) and stayed there. Explicitly asked whether the OTHER six B members touched in step 1's neighborhood (code-reviewer, fastapi-reviewer, a11y-architect, functional-test-reviewer, architect, code-architect) should also go unconditional; operator chose to leave those six exactly as they already were (proper stack-tag/path triggers, never part of A to begin with) -- confirming their existing domain scoping is intentional, not an oversight. S_opt_in_only.policy: NEVER automatic. Spawn ONLY on the operator's explicit request.
S_opt_in_only.on_signal: Flag the unit as 'security-reviewer recommended' in the report -- do not spawn.
S_opt_in_only.operator_rule: Set 2026-08-03. Overrides any earlier advice to auto-run security passes on connectors / training_servers / auth paths.

A_baseline.policy: ALWAYS, on every code unit. Exactly 2 lenses: one language reviewer (resolved by extension) + silent-failure-hunter.
A_baseline.rationale: silent-failure-hunter is not speculative -- it is the lens that caught the real bugs in the 2026-08 audit. (Briefly moved to B_domain_triggered on 2026-08-05, then restored the same day once the operator flagged that B's 'never just-in-case' policy meant an unmatched unit got zero baseline coverage -- see _meta.regrouped_2026_08_05.)

B_domain_triggered.policy: Spawn ONLY when a deterministic trigger actually fires in the unit. Never 'just in case'.

C_structural_entrypoint.policy: Entry-point units only (repo src root, main/orchestrator, wiring modules) -- typically 4-5 units, never all of them. Architectural judgement does not scale to a 5-file leaf directory.
C_structural_entrypoint.status: Intentionally empty as of 2026-08-04 (operator decision, option 1 of 3 offered). architect/code-architect moved to B; ml-engineer/database-reviewer/seo-specialist moved to T. The policy text above is kept as a template in case a future agent genuinely needs entry-point-only semantics -- it is not a bug that this list is empty.

notes.pr-test-analyzer: ONLY for an actual pull request. Outside a PR its diff framing does not apply -- use functional-test-reviewer instead.
notes.tdd-guide: Only when writing a NEW feature test-first, not when auditing existing code.

E_deferred_style.policy: Do NOT spawn during an audit. Separate low-priority pass only. These produce NIT/style, not BLOCKER/MAJOR -- the cheapest finding class per token spent.

R_reactive_on_failure.policy: Spawn ONLY in response to a real failure or a live-state question. Never during static review.

N_recon.policy: One call BEFORE triage on T3/T4 plans, to enumerate real files + domains. Cuts 30-50% of just-in-case agents.

P_planning.policy: Reviews a PROPOSED PLAN, not existing code. Do NOT include in a code audit -- these agents evaluate phase sequencing and scope, they do not find bugs in files.
P_planning.note: architect has a dual role: B_domain_triggered for code (moved from C 2026-08-04), P_planning for plans.

T_task_scoped.policy: Only when doing that exact task.

F_excluded_by_stack.policy: COMPUTED, never hardcoded. Any agent whose required stack tag is absent from the project's stack_profile is excluded. flutter-reviewer is F for a Python project and A for a Flutter one.

language_reviewer_slot._comment: Resolves the A_baseline language lens. Most-specific wins: a project-level agent of the same name overrides the global one (e.g. AI trading's python-reviewer adds a cp1252/non-ASCII check). Briefly marked SUPERSEDED on 2026-08-05 when A_baseline went empty; restored the same day -- see _meta.regrouped_2026_08_05.
language_reviewer_slot.no_framework_override: A framework does NOT replace the language lens. A FastAPI file is still Python and still needs python-reviewer; fastapi-reviewer is an ADDITIONAL Group B specialist, not a substitute. (Design fixed 2026-08-03 after the rqdo-platform survey -- a 100%-Python FastAPI repo would have lost its Python lens entirely under the old override.)

per_unit_algorithm: 1. Load the project's stack_profile -> anything requiring an absent tag goes to F_excluded.
2. Group A: resolve the language-reviewer slot by extension (project-level override wins) + silent-failure-hunter. Always 2.
3. Group B: evaluate each trigger against the unit's paths / imports / content. Add only those that actually fire.
4. Bundle A + fired-B into ONE prompt for the unit -- not one spawn per lens.
5. Group C: only if the unit is an entrypoint/orchestrator -- a separate, additional call.
6. Group D: replaces the roster entirely for tests/ units.
7. Groups E / R / T / P / S: not spawned by this algorithm. S is flagged-only; the rest need their own explicit trigger or operator request.

risk_routing.principle: Risk requires an agent -> the router selects the agent -> the model policy selects the cheapest sufficient model and effort. An agent existing is never a reason to invoke it. Triggers are evaluated by code (path globs, imports), never by an extra LLM triage call.
risk_routing.opus: Never automatic. Per-run operator consent, effort=high only, xhigh forbidden. No consent receipt mechanism exists, so hooks/agent_model_gate.py fails closed.

R0.change: trivial edit: typo, comment, formatting, docs-only, rename without behavior change

R1.change: focused change in one unit with one dominant risk

R3.change: critical: money, auth/tenancy, data loss or migration, privacy, financial, release gate

reviewers.rule: smallest complete panel that covers every material risk surface from the risk map

R3.adjudicator: only for a genuine BLOCKER/MAJOR disagreement between reviewers

T2.use: ordinary implementation, language review, functional checks

T4.use: security-critical, privacy, financial risk, red-team, adjudication

risk_routing.note: Effort is fixed per agent definition (the Agent tool has no per-call effort). Project-level critical roles (financial, privacy, adjudicator) declare T4 in their own frontmatter.
